name_en: Totsukawa sanma zushi — vinegared Pacific saury pressed onto sushi rice, or salt-fermented for New Year
summary_ja: 十津川村に伝わるサンマの寿司で、北部は塩と飯を漬け込んで長期発酵させるなれずし、南部は合わせ酢で締めて酢飯にのせる押し寿司と、村内でも作り方が分かれる。熊野灘を南下する脂の少ないサンマを使うという。
summary_en: A Pacific saury sushi from Totsukawa Village that splits into two styles even within the village: the north salt-cures and ferments the fish with rice into a nare-zushi, while the south cures it in vinegar and presses it onto sushi rice. It is said to use lean saury that has swum south through the Kumano Sea.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Ayu zushi — sweetfish pressed whole atop vinegared rice
summary_ja: 吉野川流域で作られる、アユを姿のまま酢飯にのせて押した寿司。川の石の藻を食べて育つアユは「香魚」と呼ばれ、歌舞伎の演目に登場する鮨屋が奈良に実在したことから知られるようになったとされる。
summary_en: A whole sweetfish pressed onto vinegared rice, made along the Yoshino River. Sweetfish, raised on river-stone algae, are called kogyo, 'fragrant fish,' and the sushi is said to have become known in part because a sushi shop featured in a kabuki play actually existed in Nara.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
